listen.explanationKey: How can people become United States citizens?
facts: There are three ways to become a U.S. citizen.

Being born in the United States, under the conditions in the 14th Amendment. Naturalizing: applying, passing the interview and test, and taking the Oath. Deriving citizenship, under conditions set by Congress, for example from a parent.
Which way fits a person depends on their own story. For questions about your own case, talk to a lawyer first.

newWords.meaning: to become a citizen after applying
to get something from someone else, like a parent

story.say: There are three ways to become a U.S. citizen.

help.simpler: People can become citizens in three different ways.
help.example: The three ways are: being born here, naturalizing and deriving citizenship.
help.why: The test asks how people can become U.S. citizens.

story.say: One way is being born in the United States, under the conditions in the 14th Amendment.

help.simpler: Most people born in the United States are citizens from birth.
help.why: “Be born in the United States” is one answer on the test.

story.say: Another way is to naturalize: apply, pass the interview and test, and take the Oath.

help.simpler: Naturalizing means becoming a citizen after being born somewhere else.
help.example: The civics test in this app is part of naturalizing.
help.why: “Naturalize” is another answer on the test.

check.prompt: Tap the way that includes an interview and a test.

story.say: A third way is deriving citizenship, under conditions set by Congress, for example from a parent.

help.simpler: Some people get citizenship through a parent, under rules made by Congress.
help.example: For example, some children become citizens when a parent naturalizes.
help.why: “Derive citizenship” is the third answer on the test.

story.say: Which way fits a person depends on their own story.

help.example: Two people from the same country may have different paths.
help.why: This app explains the test. It cannot tell you which way fits you.

story.say: For questions about your own case, talk to a lawyer first.

help.simpler: A lawyer can look at your own situation.
help.example: Free or low-cost legal help is listed in Free help near you.
help.why: Only a lawyer or an accredited representative should give advice about your case.

writeIt.sentence: People come here to be citizens.

listen.explanationKey: Name two promises that new citizens make in the Oath of Allegiance.
facts: New citizens take the Oath of Allegiance at the end of naturalization.
They promise to give up loyalty to other countries, defend the Constitution and obey the laws of the United States. They also promise to serve in the military or help the nation if needed.
When we say the Pledge of Allegiance, we show loyalty to the United States and the flag.

newWords.meaning: staying true to someone or something

story.say: New citizens take the Oath of Allegiance at the end of naturalization.

help.simpler: At a ceremony, new citizens say the Oath of Allegiance out loud.
help.example: This photo shows people taking the Oath at a ceremony in 1979.
help.why: The test asks you to name two promises from the Oath.

story.say: In the Oath, they make promises to the United States.

help.simpler: The Oath is a set of promises.
help.example: Four of the promises are in the picture.
help.why: You need to name two of them on the test.

story.say: They promise to give up loyalty to other countries.

help.simpler: They promise that their loyalty now belongs to the United States.
help.example: “Loyalty” means being faithful and true to someone or something.
help.why: “Give up loyalty to other countries” is one answer on the test.

check.statement: In the Oath, new citizens promise to give up loyalty to other countries.

story.say: They promise to defend the Constitution and obey the laws of the United States.

help.simpler: They promise to protect the Constitution and follow U.S. laws.
help.example: Obeying the law means following the rules, like everyone else.
help.why: “Defend the Constitution” and “Obey the laws of the United States” are two answers.

check.prompt: Tap the promise about the Constitution.

story.say: They also promise to serve in the military or help the nation if needed.

help.simpler: If the country needs help, they promise to serve.
help.example: Helping could mean military service or important work for the nation.
help.why: “Serve in the military (if needed)” and “Serve the nation (if needed)” are more answers.

story.say: When we say the Pledge of Allegiance, we show loyalty to the United States and the flag.

help.simpler: The Pledge is a short promise of loyalty that many people say.
help.example: Students in many schools say the Pledge in the morning.
help.why: The test asks what we show loyalty to: the United States and the flag.

check.prompt: What do we show loyalty to when we say the Pledge of Allegiance?
choices: The United States and the flag
